ownership.quote: The company went public on the New York Stock Exchange in 2019 under the ticker symbol NET.

stage.quote: On August 15, 2019, Cloudflare submitted its S-1 filing for an initial public offering on the New York Stock Exchange under the stock ticker NET. It opened for public trading on September 13, 2019, at $15 per share.
stage.note: Cloudflare Inc. (NYSE: NET) has traded publicly since September 2019; Browser Run / Kitesurf is a product within Cloudflare's Workers developer platform, not a separately funded entity.

total_funding_usd.basis: Aggregator figure (Crunchbase-style total of disclosed pre-IPO VC rounds, including the $150M round reported by San Francisco Business Times/TechCrunch in March 2019) commonly cited for Cloudflare's total private funding before its September 2019 IPO; no single primary source itemizing the full round-by-round total was independently re-verified in this pass.
total_funding_usd.quote: Cloudflare's $150 million funding round puts its IPO plans in question (San Francisco Business Times, March 12, 2019)

last_round.quote: Cloudflare's $150 million funding round puts its IPO plans in question (San Francisco Business Times, March 12, 2019)

revenue.basis: Cloudflare, Inc. 2025 Annual Report (Form 10-K), as summarized on Wikipedia's company infobox

note: Cloudflare Browser Run (including the Kitesurf beta engine) is a product line inside Cloudflare's Workers developer platform, not an independently funded company. Ownership/funding/stage fields describe Cloudflare, Inc. as a whole (public, NYSE: NET since 2019); revenue figure is company-wide, not broken out for Browser Run specifically. In May 2026 Cloudflare announced cutting ~1,100 positions (~20% of workforce) amid AI-driven restructuring, alongside record Q1 2026 revenue of $639.8M.
